a reinforcement learner that uses an intrinsic reward signal based on physiological responses of the human autonomic nervous system learns faster, makes less errors, and is more efficient than a learner that does not use this intrinsic reward signal.

the physiological responses of the body can serve as a proxy for reward functions in reinforcement learning tasks and can improve the sample efficiency and reduce the number and magnitude of collisions in simulated driving tasks.
